text_html: A 26-year-old man comes to the clinic for a routine health maintenance examination. He has no history of serious illness. He is a bodybuilder and uses anabolic steroids daily. He takes no other medications. Temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 72/min, respirations are 14/min, and blood pressure is 136/82 mm Hg. Physical examination shows testicular atrophy. The most likely cause of the findings in this patient is decreased serum concentration of which of the following hormones?
explanation_html:
Educational Objective: Exogenous anabolic steroid use suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, leading to testicular atrophy from decreased luteinizing hormone stimulation of testosterone production.

Evaluation: The patient has testicular atrophy in the setting of chronic anabolic steroid use, which provides supraphysiologic androgen concentrations. These androgens exert negative feedback at the hypothalamus and pituitary, suppressing gonadotropin release. Decreased gonadotropin signaling leads to decreased intratesticular testosterone and impaired spermatogenesis, resulting in testicular shrinkage.

Definition: Luteinizing hormone stimulates Leydig cells in the testes to produce testosterone, which is required for maintenance of testicular size and function. Exogenous anabolic steroids mimic testosterone and suppress gonadotropin-releasing hormone secretion, leading to decreased luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone release. Loss of luteinizing hormone decreases endogenous testosterone production within the testes, causing testicular atrophy. This mechanism underlies infertility and hypogonadism in anabolic steroid users.

Prevention: Avoidance of exogenous anabolic steroid use prevents suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.

Treatment: Discontinuation of anabolic steroids allows gradual recovery of gonadotropin secretion and testicular function, though recovery may be incomplete in cases of prolonged use.

Differential: Primary testicular failure causes increased gonadotropins rather than suppression, and adrenal androgen abnormalities do not directly regulate testicular size.

Incorrect Answers: A, B, and C.

Choice A: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate is incorrect. This adrenal androgen contributes minimally to testicular testosterone production and is not responsible for maintaining testicular size.

Choice B: Estrogen is incorrect. Estrogen concentrations may rise due to peripheral aromatization of anabolic steroids but do not directly regulate Leydig cell stimulation or testicular volume.

Choice C: Follicle-stimulating hormone is incorrect. Follicle-stimulating hormone primarily stimulates Sertoli cells and spermatogenesis, whereas loss of luteinizing hormone–driven testosterone production is the main cause of testicular atrophy.
